name: Minimal Monochrome UI
description: Black/white + 1 neutral accent. Strong typographic hierarchy, generous whitespace, crisp dividers.
implementation: Use 2 font sizes + 2 weights. 8pt spacing system. 1px hairline borders (#E5E7EB). Accent only for primary actions.
use_cases: Code dashboards, admin tools, docs sites, dev productivity apps.
do_examples: Do: Use 1 accent color for buttons/links. Do: Keep line-length 60–80 chars. Do: Prefer icons with consistent stroke.
dont_examples: Don’t: Add gradients/shadows everywhere. Don’t: Use 4+ font families. Don’t: Mix border radii randomly.

name: Neo-Brutalist Blocks
description: Bold flat colors, thick outlines, chunky spacing, intentionally ‘raw’ layout with playful geometry.
implementation: 2–3 vivid fills, 2–4px black stroke, hard shadows (offset, no blur). Use grid but allow intentional misalignment.
use_cases: Landing pages, hackathon projects, playful SaaS marketing, portfolio sites.
do_examples: Do: Use thick outlines consistently. Do: Keep typography bold and simple. Do: Use geometric shapes as containers.
dont_examples: Don’t: Pair with delicate serif body text. Don’t: Use subtle gradients. Don’t: Make everything misaligned—pick focal moments.

name: Soft Skeuomorphic (Modern)
description: Tactile surfaces with subtle depth; looks physical but restrained and contemporary.
implementation: Soft shadows (low opacity), subtle highlights, 8–16px radius, muted palette. Use layered cards and inset controls.
use_cases: Music apps, settings panels, consumer apps needing warmth and approachability.
do_examples: Do: Use 2 shadow layers (ambient + key). Do: Keep contrast accessible. Do: Use consistent radii.
dont_examples: Don’t: Overdo embossing. Don’t: Use harsh drop shadows. Don’t: Reduce text contrast to ‘look soft’.

name: Glassmorphism Lite
description: Frosted glass panels over rich backgrounds; airy, modern, tech-forward.
implementation: Use translucent surfaces (e.g., 10–20% white), backdrop blur, 1px light border, strong background imagery/gradient.
use_cases: Media players, fintech dashboards, hero sections, modals and overlays.
do_examples: Do: Increase background contrast behind glass. Do: Use blur sparingly. Do: Add border for separation.
dont_examples: Don’t: Put long paragraphs on glass. Don’t: Stack many glass layers. Don’t: Rely on blur instead of contrast.

name: Nordic Calm
description: Muted cool palette, minimal ornament, calm rhythm; ‘Scandi’ clarity.
implementation: Cool neutrals, soft blue/teal accents, thin strokes, large padding. Use simple icons and calm type.
use_cases: Health, wellbeing, productivity, B2B apps that need trust and calm.
do_examples: Do: Use low-saturation accents. Do: Keep components simple. Do: Use consistent spacing and alignment.
dont_examples: Don’t: Add loud brand colors. Don’t: Use heavy shadows. Don’t: Mix many icon styles.

name: High-Contrast Dark Mode
description: Dark UI with clear elevation and readable contrast; optimized for long sessions.
implementation: Near-black surfaces (#0B0F14), 2–3 elevation layers, text contrast >= WCAG AA, accent color for focus states.
use_cases: Developer tools, terminals, analytics, creative software.
do_examples: Do: Use slightly lighter cards for elevation. Do: Use distinct focus rings. Do: Use muted borders.
dont_examples: Don’t: Use pure black everywhere. Don’t: Use low-contrast gray text. Don’t: Over-saturate accents.

name: Pastel Gradient Pop
description: Cheerful pastel gradients paired with clean UI; modern and friendly.
implementation: Use 1–2 gradient areas (hero/background). Keep UI controls solid. Pair with rounded corners and simple type.
use_cases: Consumer apps, onboarding flows, youth brands, marketing sites.
do_examples: Do: Limit gradients to large areas. Do: Keep buttons solid for clarity. Do: Maintain contrast for text.
dont_examples: Don’t: Put gradients inside every component. Don’t: Use neon + pastel together. Don’t: Let gradients reduce legibility.

name: Editorial Serif + Sans
description: Magazine-like layout using serif headlines and sans body; sophisticated and content-first.
implementation: Serif display for H1/H2, sans for body. Use baseline grid, generous margins, subtle rules and captions.
use_cases: Blogs, long-form docs, portfolios, brand storytelling pages.
do_examples: Do: Use limited type scale. Do: Keep body line-height 1.5–1.7. Do: Use image captions.
dont_examples: Don’t: Use more than 2 typefaces. Don’t: Overuse italics. Don’t: Compress whitespace.

name: Retro Terminal
description: CRT/terminal vibes: monospace, scanlines optional, green/amber on dark.
implementation: Monospace font, limited palette (green/amber/gray), pixel icons, subtle noise. Use box-drawing borders.
use_cases: CLI tools, dev-themed sites, playful demos, security tools marketing.
do_examples: Do: Keep interactions modern (buttons, focus states). Do: Use monospace consistently. Do: Use subtle noise.
dont_examples: Don’t: Make everything tiny. Don’t: Sacrifice accessibility. Don’t: Use too many effects (scanlines + glitch + noise).

name: Material-ish Cards
description: Card-based layout with clear elevation and motion; familiar and scalable.
implementation: Use 2–3 elevation levels, consistent shadows, 4–8px radii, clear iconography. Motion: 150–250ms ease.
use_cases: Dashboards, content libraries, mobile-first web apps.
do_examples: Do: Use elevation to show hierarchy. Do: Keep motion consistent. Do: Use clear card spacing.
dont_examples: Don’t: Use random shadow styles. Don’t: Over-animate. Don’t: Nest too many cards.

name: Data-Dense Professional
description: Compact, information-forward UI with strong grid and typographic clarity.
implementation: Tight spacing, table-first components, restrained color. Use zebra rows, sticky headers, compact filters.
use_cases: Ops dashboards, finance tools, CRM/ERP, monitoring.
do_examples: Do: Use alignment and spacing to reduce visual noise. Do: Provide hover/selected row states. Do: Use icons sparingly.
dont_examples: Don’t: Waste vertical space. Don’t: Rely on color alone for status. Don’t: Use oversized illustrations.

name: Playful Rounded
description: Friendly shapes, rounded corners, warm palette; approachable and human.
implementation: 12–24px radii, soft shadows, warm accents, chunky buttons. Use simple illustrations and friendly microcopy.
use_cases: Education, kids apps, onboarding, community products.
do_examples: Do: Keep a consistent radius system. Do: Use warm neutrals. Do: Use playful but readable typography.
dont_examples: Don’t: Mix sharp and round components. Don’t: Overuse stickers/badges. Don’t: Use childish fonts for body text.
